subject: Information Theory
title: Why Gaussian Is Special
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Gaussian Is Special usable.

hook.text: The bell curve shows up everywhere—heights, test scores, noise. Shannon's theory explains why.

buildup.text: Among all distributions with a fixed mean and variance, the Gaussian has the highest entropy.

discovery.text: It commits to nothing beyond what you measured. Any other shape smuggles in extra assumptions.

twist.text: This is why engineers model noise as Gaussian by default. It's the honest admission of maximum ignorance.

climax.text: The central limit theorem and max entropy converge: sums of random variables approach the Gaussian for the same reason.

punchline.text: Maximum ignorance with known spread: it's a bell curve.

quiz.question: Why does the Gaussian distribution appear so often?
options: It maximizes entropy for a given mean and variance
